tafamidis_recommendations.recommendation_hereditary: Tafamidis is recommended in patients with genetic testing proven hTTR-CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, cardiovascular (CV) hospitalization and mortality.
tafamidis_recommendations.recommendation_wildtype: Tafamidis is recommended in patients with wtTTR-CA and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality.

section_14.8_adult_congenital_heart_dise.overview: Management of adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) reviewed in ESC guideline. Heart failure (HF) is a common problem affecting ~20–50% of ACHD population and an important cause of death.
section_14.8_adult_congenital_heart_dise.pathophysiology: Cardiac dysfunction in ACHD often differs from acquired heart disease (examples: systemic right ventricle, failing subpulmonary ventricle, single ventricle, surgery-related injury, chronic pressure/volume overload, hypertrophy or non-compaction induced by gene mutations).
section_14.8_adult_congenital_heart_dise.evidence_and_recommendations: Extrapolation of current HF treatment guidelines to ACHD patients is not always appropriate. Available data on HF treatments in ACHD are often inconclusive and derived from small cohorts; ACHD-specific recommendations are mostly based on clinical experience or position statements.
section_14.8_adult_congenital_heart_dise.management_principles: ACHD patients with HF should be referred to expert/specialized centres. Specific guidelines for medical treatment of chronic HF in ACHD are lacking; practitioners should follow current HF guidelines while recognizing uncertainties (including whether long-term use of neurohormonal modulators affects outcomes in ACHD).
section_14.8_adult_congenital_heart_dise.table_summary: Table 36: ACHD patients with chronic HF should be referred to specialized centres.

genes.context: Page recommends tafamidis for patients with genetic testing proven hTTR-CA and wtTTR-CA; abbreviations define hTTR as hereditary transthyretin and wtTTR as wild-type transthyretin, linking TTR to transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
